## Claims
- [source-backed] For \(v_{r,s,t,n}\), \(1\le t\le r,s\le n\), \(t>r+s-n\), and \(i=s-t+1,\ j=r-t+1,\ a=\min(n-r-i,r-j),\ b=\min(i,j)\); a valid \((n,r,i,j,a,b,N)\) has all coordinates positive and satisfies \(r<n,\ a+j\le r,\ a+i\le n-r,\ b\le i,j,\ N\le ab\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 187-235; 300-304]
- [proved] The original and parameter-conjugated cores and both upper shapes satisfy all stated partition, containment, ambient-box, positivity, and valid-tuple conditions; the \(a=0\) boundary has singleton families and admits no valid \(N\).

## Strategy
Put \(q=n-r\) and
\[
(r^\vee,s^\vee,t^\vee)=(q,n-s,q-s+t).
\]
First \(r,s<n\): if \(r=n\), then \(t>r+s-n=s\), contradicting \(t\le s\); similarly \(s=n\) contradicts \(t\le r\). Hence \(1\le q<n\).

Moreover,
\[
t^\vee=q-s+t\ge1,\quad t^\vee\le q\ (t\le s),\quad
t^\vee\le n-s\ (t\le r),
\]
and
\[
t^\vee-(r^\vee+s^\vee-n)=t>0.
\]
Thus the conjugated triple is bigrassmannian. Its parameters are
\[
i^\vee=j,\qquad j^\vee=i,\qquad a^\vee=a,\qquad b^\vee=b.
\]
Also
\[
q-i=t^\vee-1\ge0,\qquad r-j=t-1\ge0,
\]
so
\[
i\le q,\quad j\le r,\quad i+a\le q,\quad j+a\le r,\quad b\le i,j. \tag{*}
\]

Assume first \(a\ge1\). Write \(B=q^r\) and \(B^\vee=r^q\). Every displayed height is the number of positive parts.

| ambient box | shape | width | height | partition condition | core-containment | ambient-box inequalities |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|---|
| \(B=q^r\) | original core \(i^j\) | \(i\) | \(j\) | \(i,j\ge1\) | itself | \(i\le q,\ j\le r\) |
| \(B=q^r\) | original lower upper \((i^j,b^a)\) | \(\max(i,b)=i\) | \(j+a\) | \(b\le i\) | its first \(j\) rows are \(i^j\) | \(i\le q,\ j+a\le r\) |
| \(B=q^r\) | original right upper \(((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\) | \(i+a\) | \(j\) | \(b\le j\) | first \(b\) rows have length \(i+a\ge i\), remaining \(j-b\) have length \(i\) | \(i+a\le q,\ j\le r\) |
| \(B^\vee=r^q\) | conjugated core \(j^i\) | \(j\) | \(i\) | \(i,j\ge1\) | itself | \(j\le r,\ i\le q\) |
| \(B^\vee=r^q\) | conjugated lower upper \((j^i,b^a)\) | \(\max(j,b)=j\) | \(i+a\) | \(b\le j\) | its first \(i\) rows are \(j^i\) | \(j\le r,\ i+a\le q\) |
| \(B^\vee=r^q\) | conjugated right upper \(((j+a)^b,j^{i-b})\) | \(j+a\) | \(i\) | \(b\le i\) | first \(b\) rows have length \(j+a\ge j\), remaining \(i-b\) have length \(j\) | \(j+a\le r,\ i\le q\) |

All table inequalities are instances of \((*)\). Hence every partition in each interval from the listed core to its listed upper shape lies in the indicated ambient box.

Partition conjugation gives both exact correspondences:
\[
\{\lambda:i^j\subseteq\lambda\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}'
 =
\{\mu:j^i\subseteq\mu\subseteq((j+a)^b,j^{i-b})\},
\]
\[
\{\lambda:i^j\subseteq\lambda\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\}'
 =
\{\mu:j^i\subseteq\mu\subseteq(j^i,b^a)\}.
\]
Indeed, transposing an appended \(b^a\) rectangle yields a right appendage of width \(a\) in the first \(b\) rows, and transposition is an inclusion-preserving involution.

For \(a\ge1\) and \(1\le N\le ab\), the original tuple satisfies, explicitly,
\[
n,r,i,j,a,b,N\ge1,\quad r<n,\quad
a+j\le r,\quad a+i\le q=n-r,
\]
\[
b\le i,\quad b\le j,\quad 1\le N,\quad N\le ab.
\]
The conjugated tuple
\[
(n,r^\vee,i^\vee,j^\vee,a^\vee,b^\vee,N)=(n,q,j,i,a,b,N)
\]
satisfies
\[
n,q,j,i,a,b,N\ge1,\quad q<n,\quad
a+i\le q,\quad a+j\le r=n-q,
\]
\[
b\le j,\quad b\le i,\quad 1\le N,\quad N\le ab.
\]
Thus both are valid.

Finally, if \(a=0\), then
\[
a=0\iff q-i=0\ \text{or}\ r-j=0
\iff i=q\ \text{or}\ j=r.
\]
These alternatives interchange under conjugation. Since \(b\le i,j\),
\[
(i^j,b^0)=i^j,\qquad ((i+0)^b,i^{j-b})=i^j,
\]
and
\[
(j^i,b^0)=j^i,\qquad ((j+0)^b,j^{i-b})=j^i.
\]
Thus all four intervals are singleton cores. No valid \(N\) exists, since
\[
1\le N\le ab=0
\]
is impossible.

This scoped admissibility certificate is thereby established; no parent-theorem conclusion is used.
